extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and practitioners studying health misinformation, social media video analysis, multimodal NLP/CV, and dataset/annotation builders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for creating and analyzing a multimodal corpus of short-form social media videos about nutrition and supplements, including which features to annotate and how to validate annotations. Emphasizes visual authority signals, presenter attributes, narrative techniques, monetization cues, and a transparent annotation pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority cues such as titles, slides and charts, and certificates appear in videos and constitute visual signals of credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code for the presence of explicit visuals that claim or imply expertise or institutional backing (e.g., on-screen titles, slides/charts, certificates). Note that the paper finds these visuals frequently co-occur with persuasive elements; do not assume such visuals indicate restraint or accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenter attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes of the presenter including number (e.g., single presenter), demeanor (e.g., confident), and setting (e.g., studio or home versus clinical contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate presenter count, expressed confidence/authority, and setting. The study reports a dominant pattern of a confident single presenter in studio or home settings and that clinical contexts are rare — use those categories when coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative strategies / persuasive elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative techniques used to persuade viewers, including jargon, references, appeals to fear or urgency, critiques of mainstream medicine, and conspiratorial framings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark occurrences of jargon, explicit references to sources, emotional appeals (fear/urgency), oppositional critiques of mainstream medicine, and conspiratorial claims. Treat these as rhetorical strategies that may combine with authority signals rather than as independent proof of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement and monetization cues
rubrics_metrics.description: Signals of monetization and audience engagement such as sales links, calls to subscribe, and other commercial or follower-building prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate visible or spoken monetization behaviors (e.g., product links, promo codes, 'subscribe' or 'follow' calls). The paper notes these monetization cues frequently occur alongside authority and persuasive elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and science-like visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of references (citations or claims of research) and visuals that evoke scientific authority (e.g., charts, lab-like imagery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record presence of explicit references to studies or scientific-sounding visuals. Important: the authors find that references and science-like visuals often travel with emotive and oppositional narratives rather than signalling caution — annotate both the visual/textual form and the rhetorical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-occurrence of cues (relational analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical attention to how authority cues, persuasive elements, and monetization co-occur within videos (patterns of association between features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing or scoring videos, examine and report feature co-occurrence patterns (e.g., titles + fear appeals + sales links) rather than only marginal prevalence. The study emphasizes that authority cues commonly accompany persuasive and monetized content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-platform corpus composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus construction across platforms and sample size: the study assembled 152 public videos from TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sampling covers multiple short-form and long-form video platforms to capture cross-platform variation; document platform sources and corpus size. Use platform-specific considerations (e.g., TikTok vertical format) when annotating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent annotation pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A principled, transparent annotation pipeline integrating automatic speech recognition (ASR), principled frame selection, and a multimodal model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an explicit, reproducible pipeline that includes: ASR to obtain transcripts, clearly documented criteria for selecting frames for visual analysis, and methods for fusing audio/transcript/visual modalities. Provide enough detail so others can reproduce preprocessing and feature extraction steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) for transcript generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of automatic speech recognition to extract spoken content as part of the multimodal annotation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ASR and document model/version and error characteristics; verify ASR outputs where possible because transcript quality affects coding of narrative strategies and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principled frame selection
rubrics_metrics.description: A method for selecting representative frames from videos for visual analysis (referred to as 'principled frame selection').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and document criteria for which frames are chosen (e.g., speaker shots, frames with on-screen text/graphics). Use consistent rules so visual-feature annotations are comparable across videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal modeling and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporating a multimodal model to combine audio/transcript and visual features for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use models or methods that explicitly fuse modalities; document model architecture and inputs. Multimodal integration is central to capturing authority signals that may be distributed across text, speech, and visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human verification and inter-annotator agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Human verification on a stratified subsample to validate automatic/machine annotations, with reporting of agreement levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform human checks on a stratified subset of the corpus and report inter-annotator agreement metrics (the paper reports 'strong agreement'). Use stratified sampling to ensure validation covers major subgroups (platforms, topical clusters, etc.).
